arabic_blocks: [1132] حدثنا حفص بن عمر حدثنا شعبة قال: أخبرني عبد الملك عن قزعة قال: سمعت أبا سعيد رضى الله تعالى عنه أربعا قال: سمعت من النبي ﷺ وكان غزا مع النبي ﷺ ثنتي عشرة غزوة ح حدثنا علي حدثنا سفيان عن الزهري عن سعيد عن أبي هريرة رضى الله تعالى عنه عن النبي ﷺ قال لا تشد الرحال إلا إلى ثلاثة مساجد المسجد الحرام ومسجد الرسول ﷺ ومسجد الأقصى
english_blocks: Hafs ibn ‘Umar related to us. Shu‘bah related to us. He said: ‘Abd al-Malik informed me, from Qaza‘ah, who said:

I heard Abu Sa‘id, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, relate four things. He said: “I heard from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.” He had gone on twelve expeditions with the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace.

Another route: ‘Ali related to us. Sufyan related to us, from al-Zuhri, from Sa‘id, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, who said:
Journeys are not to be undertaken except to three mosques: the Sacred Mosque, the Mosque of the Messenger, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and al-Aqsa Mosque.

english_blocks: ‘Abdullah ibn Yusuf related to us. He said: Malik informed us, from Zayd ibn Rabah and ‘Ubaydullah ibn Abi ‘Abdullah al-Agharr, from Abu ‘Abdullah al-Agharr, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:
A prayer in this mosque of mine is better than a thousand prayers elsewhere, except the Sacred Mosque.

english_blocks: Ya‘qub ibn Ibrahim related to us. Ibn ‘Ulayyah related to us. Ayyub informed us, from Nafi‘:

Ibn ‘Umar, may Allah Most High be pleased with them both, did not pray Duha except on two days: the day he arrived in Mecca, for he used to arrive there in the forenoon, circumambulate the House and then pray two rak‘ahs behind the Maqam; and the day he came to the Quba Mosque. He used to come to it every Saturday. When he entered the mosque, he disliked leaving it until he had prayed in it. He said: He used to relate that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, would visit it riding and on foot.

He said: He used to say, “I only do as I saw my companions doing. I do not prevent anyone from praying at whatever hour he wishes of the night or day, except that you should not deliberately seek out sunrise or sunset.”

english_blocks: Abu al-Walid related to us. Shu‘bah related to us, from ‘Abd al-Malik: I heard Qaza‘ah, the mawla of Ziyad, who said:
I heard Abu Sa‘id al-Khudri, may Allah Most High be pleased with him, relate four things from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, which pleased and delighted me. He said:

A woman is not to travel for two days unless her husband or a mahram is with her. And there is no fasting on two days: al-Fitr and al-Adha. And there is no prayer after two prayers: after the morning prayer until the sun rises, and after ‘Asr until it sets. And journeys are not to be undertaken except to three mosques: the Sacred Mosque, al-Aqsa Mosque and my mosque.
